title: Duality between the level statistics of Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrices
authors: Ze Chen, Zhenyu Xiao, Yifei Liu, Shinsei Ryu
abstract: Random matrix theory describes complex quantum systems statistically, with symmetry as its organizing principle. We uncover an exact duality between the level statistics of Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrices in the large-$N$ (matrix size) limit. It acts class by class: the two replica partition functions, given by fermionic nonlinear $σ$ models, are related by analytic continuation. Applied to the three Wigner--Dyson classes, the duality yields the universal bulk eigenvalue pair-correlation functions of non-Hermitian random matrices. This establishes a non-Hermitian counterpart of Dyson's threefold way, organized by transposition symmetry: generic complex, complex symmetric, and complex self-dual matrices. The dissipative spectral form factors of these classes follow in closed form as well. Applied to the seven nonstandard Altland--Zirnbauer classes, the duality yields the exact spectral densities near the origin, the non-Hermitian hard-edge statistics. Most of these statistics were previously known only numerically. Exact diagonalization confirms the analytical predictions, and physical models demonstrate their universality. We expect these results to be the tip of a deeper correspondence between Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrix theory.
summary: This work establishes a profound mathematical duality between the eigenvalue statistics of Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrices. By relating replica partition functions via nonlinear sigma models, the authors derive universal, closed-form results for non-Hermitian spectral properties. This advances the understanding of complex quantum systems described by non-Hermitian Hamiltonians.
main_problem: The paper uncovers an exact duality connecting the level statistics of Hermitian and non-Hermitian random matrices.
main_result: This duality establishes a non-Hermitian counterpart to Dyson's threefold way, providing closed-form expressions for bulk pair-correlation functions and hard-edge spectral densities for previously intractable non-Hermitian classes.
method: The duality is derived by relating two replica partition functions, which are formulated using fermionic nonlinear sigma models and evaluated in the large-N limit.
model_or_system: The study uses random matrix theory, comparing Hermitian ensembles (governed by standard symmetries) with non-Hermitian ensembles (governed by symmetries like $	ext{TRS}^\dagger$, $	ext{PHS}$, and $	ext{Chiral Symmetry}$).
key_observables: Level statistics, including bulk eigenvalue pair-correlation functions and spectral densities near the origin (hard-edge statistics).
important_parameters: Large-$N$ limit, symmetry classes (e.g., A, $	ext{AI}^\dagger$, $	ext{AII}^\dagger$), and the replica number $n$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-$N$ limit and the mathematical framework of nonlinear sigma models derived from replica methods.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares calculated pair-correlation functions ($\pi^2 R_2(\omega)$) for non-Hermitian classes A, $	ext{AI}^\dagger$, and $	ext{AII}^\dagger$ against exact diagonalization results.
paper_structure: The paper systematically establishes the duality using sigma models, applies it to the three Wigner-Dyson classes in the bulk, and then extends the mapping to the seven nonstandard Altland-Zirnbauer classes for the hard-edge statistics.
why_interesting: The explicit connection between Hermitian and non-Hermitian spectral statistics is crucial for understanding open quantum systems, where non-Hermiticity arises naturally from coupling to an environment (dissipation).

(12), (14), and (16)], with no fitting parameters. Markers are exact-diagonalization results from 10,000 matrices of size N = 512 for classes A and AI† and N = 1024 for class AII†.

FIG. 2. Spectral densities near the origin, πR1(|z|), in the seven non-Wigner–Dyson AZ0 classes. Open circles are exact- diagonalization results from 106 Gaussian random matrices for every displayed class and topological sector, with base size N = 128; solid curves are the exact analytical densities of Table I, with no fitting parameters. The random matrix ensembles are normalized so that πR1(z) = 1 away from the spectral edge. Protected exact zero modes are excluded, and each Kramers pair in classes CII0 and DIII0 is counted once.

FIG. 4. Eigenvalue pair-correlation functions of the q = 4 non-Hermitian SYK model in classes A (Nγ = 18), AI† (Nγ = 16), and AII† (Nγ = 20), in the unfolded variables of Eq. (75). Markers are exact-diagonalization results from 105 disorder realizations per class, using eigenvalue pairs with a reference level in the central 30% of the spectrum. The solid curves are the exact analytical results of Eqs. (12), (14), and (16), with no fitting parameters.

FIG. 3. Connected dissipative spectral form factor Kc/N for classes A, AI†, and AII†. Markers are Fourier transforms of bulk eigenvalue pair-correlation functions obtained by exact diagonalization of 3 × 106 Gaussian matrices per class, with N = 128 distinct eigenvalues; solid curves are the exact large- N results in Eqs. (69), (70), and (71). (a) Full crossover to the plateau; short dashed segments show the quadratic ramps in Eq. (72). (b) Plateau deviation for class AII†; the shaded positive region displays the overshoot. (c) Algebraic tail of class AI† on logarithmic axes. Statistical errors are smaller than the markers.

FIG. 5. The BDI0 spectral density near the origin, πR1, as a function of |z| in the sectors ν = 0, 1, 2, 3 for the quadratic Lindbladian model [Eq. (77)].
